strategies.name: Baseline 8-stage all-reduce chain
strategies.desc: Directly implements the reference pattern with 8 sequential all_reduce calls, each preceded by local forward bidiagonal coupling and followed by local backward decoupling. Dispatch count = 8 all_reduce operations. Represents the simplest structural approach with minimal code complexity but no fusion or overlap opportunities.

strategies.name: Fused coupling with vectorized local ops
strategies.desc: Uses 8 all_reduce calls but pre-computes all bidiagonal coefficients and vectorizes the coupling/decoupling loops using torch slice operations or views to enable potential backend fusion of element-wise operations. Dispatch count = 8 all_reduce. Trades increased local compute planning (view creation, coefficient tensors) for reduced local-op overhead between collectives.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter + all-gather decomposition per stage
strategies.desc: Replaces each all_reduce with reduce_scatter followed by all_gather, allowing each rank to compute its own shard's coupling locally during the scatter phase, then broadcast via all_gather. Dispatch count = 16 collectives (2 per stage × 8 stages). Trades doubled collective count for smaller per-rank payload (factor of W reduction) and potential compute-communication overlap during scatter.

strategies.name: Pipelined all-reduce with async dispatch
strategies.desc: Issues multiple all_reduce operations asynchronously where dependency allows, particularly pipelining the initial all_reduce with subsequent stage preparation. Dispatch count = 8 all_reduce but with async execution model. Exploits XLA's lazy evaluation to overlap collective communication with local coupling/decoupling computation, hiding latency at the cost of increased in-flight buffer requirements.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction tree
strategies.desc:
Exploits the num_devices/cores_per_device structure to first perform intra-device reductions (within each Trainium chip's cores), then inter-device all_reduce, applying bidiagonal coupling at the device-granularity level. Dispatch count = 8 × 2 levels = 16 but with smaller cross-device payloads. Reduces cross-chip bandwidth demand by factor of cores_per_device at the cost of additional intra-chip synchronization overhead.
